papers.title: OPTIMIZING CLOUD RESOURCE ALLOCATION USING MULTI AGENT DEEP REINFORCEMENT LEARNING-BASED ADAPTIVE HHO ALGORITHM
papers.abstract: Cloud computing workloads are projected to grow by 23.1% annually, with over 80% of enterprises adopting multi-cloud strategies, creating a pressing need for optimal virtual machine (VM) resource allocation to ensure cost efficiency and performance. However, existing allocation strategies suffer from static optimization limitations and inefficient adaptation to dynamic workloads, leading to frequent resource underutilization and service delays. To address these issues, this work proposes a novel Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Adaptive Harris Hawks Optimization (MADRL-AHHO) algorithm for cloud resource allocation using the VM Resource Allocation dataset (VM-0 to VM-5 classes). Initially, the dataset is preprocessed through normalization and feature selection to reduce dimensionality and noise. Feature extraction is enhanced using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) integrated with Firefly Optimization (CNN-FFO), which is benchmarked for learning capacity and solution convergence. However, performance limitations in CNN-FFO under dynamic load conditions are overcome by integrating CNN with Adaptive Harris Hawks Optimization (CNN-AHHO), which dynamically adjusts its exploration and exploitation capabilities based on multi-agent reinforcement feedback. The agents interact with the environment to learn optimal VM allocation policies by maximizing resource utilization and minimizing SLA violations. Experimental results demonstrate that CNN-AHHO outperforms CNN-FFO and traditional machine learning methods in terms of allocation accuracy, convergence rate, and computational efficiency, thereby offering a robust and adaptive solution for cloud infrastructure management.

papers.title: Transformer-Based Scalable Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Joint Resource Optimization in Cloud–Edge–End Video Streaming Systems
papers.abstract: Cloud-edge-end (CEE) collaboration has demonstrated significant potential in video streaming analysis. However, dynamic wireless environments, lack of incentive mechanisms, and constrained resources (e.g., transmission power, bandwidth, and computing resources) remain the primary bottlenecks for achieving efficient CEE-based video processing. To address these challenges, this paper focuses on a multi-user CEE scenario with dynamic wireless channels and investigates the joint optimization of adaptive incentives, cooperative offloading, and resource allocation. We propose a novel framework, called JROC, to motivate edge devices (EDs) to participate in collaborative computation within CEE, thereby enhancing system utility. Specifically, JROC encompasses a smart contract-based adaptive incentive mechanism and an Adaptive Transformer-based multi-agent reinforcement Learning Algorithm (ATLA). The incentive mechanism leverages blockchain to ensure trustworthy and automated incentive distribution, while ATLA captures long-term dependencies and global state features among agents to guide video tasks in dynamic environments through adaptive compression, cooperative offloading, and resource allocation. Moreover, we discuss key steps for deploying the proposed algorithm in a real CEE prototype, including lightweight actor inference at the terminal side and training at the edge. Experimental results based on a real-world operator dataset show that, compared to existing methods, JROC achieves higher long-term system utility while maintaining favorable scalability, thereby validating its effectiveness in resource-constrained and under-incentivized CEE video streaming scenarios.

papers.title: Mobility-Aware Resource Allocation for mmWave IAB Networks: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Approach
papers.abstract: MmWaves have been envisioned as a promising direction to provide Gbps wireless access. However, they are susceptible to high path losses and blockages, which directional antennas can only partially mitigate. That makes mmWave networks coverage-limited, thus requiring dense deployments. Integrated access and backhaul (IAB) architectures have emerged as a cost-effective solution for network densification. Resource allocation in mmWave IAB networks must face big challenges to cope with heavy temporal dynamics, such as intermittent links caused by user mobility and blockages from moving obstacles. This makes it extremely difficult to find optimal and adaptive solutions. In this article, exploiting the distributed structure of the problem, we propose a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework to optimize user throughput via flow routing and link scheduling in mmWave IAB networks characterized by user mobility and link outages generated by moving obstacles. The proposed approach implicitly captures the environment dynamics, coordinates the interference, and manages the buffer levels of IAB relay nodes. We design different MARL components, considering full-duplex and half-duplex IAB-nodes. In addition, we provide a communication and coordination scheme for RL agents in an online training framework, addressing the feasibility issues of practical systems. Numerical results show the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

papers.title: Efficient Resource Allocation for On-Demand Mobile-Edge Cloud Computing
papers.abstract: Mobile-edge cloud computing is a new paradigm to provide cloud computing capabilities at the edge of pervasive radio access networks in close proximity to mobile users. Aiming at provisioning flexible on-demand mobile-edge cloud service, in this paper we propose a comprehensive framework consisting of a resource-efficient computation offloading mechanism for users and a joint communication and computation (JCC) resource allocation mechanism for network operator. Specifically, we first study the resource-efficient computation offloading problem for a user, in order to reduce user's resource occupation by determining its optimal communication and computation resource profile with minimum resource occupation and meanwhile satisfying the QoS constraint. We then tackle the critical problem of user admission control for JCC resource allocation, in order to properly select the set of users for resource demand satisfaction. We show the admission control problem is NP-hard, and hence develop an efficient approximation solution of a low complexity by carefully designing the user ranking criteria and rigourously derive its performance guarantee. To prevent the manipulation that some users may untruthfully report their valuations in acquiring mobile-edge cloud service, we further resort to the powerful tool of critical value approach to design truthful pricing scheme for JCC resource allocation. Extensive performance evaluation demonstrates that the proposed schemes can achieve superior performance for on-demand mobile-edge cloud computing.

summary: The literature on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for dynamic resource allocation in cloud computing emphasizes the need for adaptive and efficient strategies to address challenges in both cloud and edge environments. Key contributions include novel algorithms like Adaptive Harris Hawks Optimization and Transformer-based frameworks that enhance resource allocation under dynamic workloads. However, limitations such as static optimization strategies and untested scalability in larger networks highlight significant research gaps, particularly in integrating advanced machine learning techniques and addressing user admission control complexities.
scholarly_positioning: Existing research on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for resource allocation in cloud computing has primarily focused on static optimization techniques, which struggle to adapt to rapidly changing workloads and user demands. While novel algorithms like Adaptive Harris Hawks Optimization and Transformer-based frameworks have shown promise, they often overlook the complexities of user admission control and scalability in larger networks. This proposal addresses these unresolved tensions by introducing a hybrid MARL approach that dynamically integrates user behavior and environmental factors, thus enhancing adaptability and efficiency in resource allocation. By situating this work within the broader context of cloud and edge computing, it aims to fill critical gaps in the literature and advance the scientific understanding of real-time resource management strategies.
research_scope: This study will investigate the application of a hybrid Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework for dynamic resource allocation in cloud computing environments, specifically targeting cloud-based deep learning tasks. The evaluation period will span six months, during which the proposed MARL approach will be compared against traditional optimization algorithms and single-agent reinforcement learning methods. The primary outcome will be the efficiency of resource allocation, measured through user throughput and long-term system utility. Secondary outcomes will include scalability metrics and adaptation speed to dynamic workloads. The study will utilize simulated cloud environments and real-world user behavior datasets to ensure comprehensive analysis and validation of the proposed framework.

technical_feasibility: The proposed study is technically feasible as it primarily relies on simulated cloud environments and real-world user behavior datasets, which can be accessed without requiring open-source model access or hidden state extraction. However, it will need GPU resources for training the MARL models effectively. The study does not involve human participants, so ethics approval is not necessary. It is recommended to ensure that the real-world user behavior datasets are adequately labeled and representative of dynamic workloads. If internal representations are to be analyzed, consider using open-source models or frameworks that allow for deeper insights into the agent's decision-making process.
gap: Prior studies have demonstrated the effectiveness of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) in optimizing resource allocation in cloud computing environments; however, they treat user admission control and environmental dynamics as fixed or secondary factors, leaving unclear whether these elements significantly affect resource allocation efficiency and adaptability. This matters theoretically because understanding the interplay between user behavior and resource management can lead to more robust and scalable solutions; therefore, this study investigates the integration of user behavior adaptation and environmental factors within a hybrid MARL framework for dynamic resource allocation in cloud-based deep learning tasks.
question: How does the integration of user behavior adaptation and environmental factors within a hybrid Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning framework impact resource allocation efficiency and user throughput in dynamic cloud-based deep learning tasks compared to traditional optimization algorithms and single-agent reinforcement learning methods?
theoretical_mechanism: The proposed research investigates how the integration of user behavior adaptation (independent variable) and environmental factors (moderator) within a hybrid Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework influences resource allocation efficiency (dependent variable) and user throughput (dependent variable) in dynamic cloud-based deep learning tasks. The theoretical framework is grounded in adaptive systems theory, which posits that systems can enhance performance through feedback loops and dynamic adjustments. The causal chain suggests that user behavior adaptation and environmental factors interact to mediate the effectiveness of resource allocation strategies, leading to improved system-level outcomes such as long-term system utility and scalability metrics. Assumptions requiring empirical validation include the premise that user behavior significantly impacts resource allocation decisions and that environmental factors can be effectively integrated into the MARL framework without introducing instability in the learning process.
hypothesis: Integrating user behavior adaptation into a hybrid Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning framework will significantly improve resource allocation efficiency compared to traditional optimization algorithms, with the expected increase in user throughput acting as a mediator in dynamic cloud-based deep learning tasks.

proposal: This research proposal aims to develop a hybrid Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework for dynamic resource allocation in cloud computing, specifically targeting cloud-based deep learning tasks such as image processing and natural language processing. Key concepts include MARL, defined as a collaborative decision-making process among multiple agents, and dynamic resource allocation, which refers to the real-time distribution of computing resources based on fluctuating workloads. The study assumes technical feasibility through the use of simulated cloud environments and real-world user behavior datasets, requiring GPU resources for model training. The motivation stems from existing literature that highlights the inadequacy of static optimization techniques in addressing user admission control and environmental dynamics, which are critical for adapting to rapidly changing workloads. The identified gap is grounded in literature, as prior studies (e.g., P2 and P4) have shown limitations in scalability and adaptability, necessitating a more nuanced approach that integrates user behavior and environmental factors. The research question investigates how the integration of user behavior adaptation (independent variable) and environmental factors (moderator) within a hybrid MARL framework impacts resource allocation efficiency (dependent variable) and user throughput (dependent variable) compared to traditional optimization algorithms and single-agent reinforcement learning methods. The theoretical mechanism posits that user behavior adaptation enhances decision-making in the MARL framework, leading to improved resource allocation efficiency and user throughput through feedback loops. The falsifiable hypothesis states that integrating user behavior adaptation will significantly improve resource allocation efficiency, with increased user throughput acting as a mediator. Constructs will be operationalized using behavioral logs for user behavior adaptation, environmental condition metrics for environmental factors, and user throughput and long-term system utility metrics for resource allocation efficiency. The methodology will compare the proposed MARL approach against traditional optimization algorithms and single-agent methods, utilizing metrics such as user throughput and long-term system utility while controlling for workload intensity and user demand fluctuations. Validity will be ensured through rigorous experimental design, including controls for confounding variables like network conditions. The expected contributions include theoretical advancements in adaptive systems theory, technical innovations in MARL methodology, empirical findings from comprehensive datasets, and practical guidelines for deploying MARL systems in cloud environments. Key limitations include potential scalability issues in larger networks and the risk of poor performance under extreme dynamic conditions, which will be mitigated through hierarchical MARL structures and adaptive learning strategies.

Major weaknesses: While the novelty is clear, the proposal could benefit from a more explicit discussion of how it extends existing literature and addresses specific gaps. Next band requirements: To achieve a higher score, the proposal should articulate how its contributions uniquely advance theoretical understanding and practical applications.

The proposed methodology is realistic and utilizes appropriate baselines, but it lacks detailed controls and specific metrics for evaluating the proposed framework. Major weaknesses: Insufficient detail on the experimental design, particularly regarding how confounding variables will be controlled and evaluated. Next band requirements: More comprehensive details on experimental controls, metrics, and potential confounds are necessary for a higher score.

rubric_scores.level: 12-13: strong literature grounding with good comparative analysis
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal engages with relevant literature and identifies gaps, but it primarily summarizes existing work rather than critically analyzing it. Major weaknesses: Lack of depth in synthesizing prior work and insufficient identification of unresolved tensions within the literature. Next band requirements: A more critical synthesis of literature that situates the proposed research within broader debates and highlights specific unresolved issues is needed.

rubric_scores.level: 7-8: approaching PhD-level with some shallow areas
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal demonstrates some theoretical sophistication but lacks depth in discussing the mechanisms behind the proposed framework and its implications. Major weaknesses: Limited discussion of the broader implications of the research and insufficient exploration of potential limitations and failure cases. Next band requirements: A deeper exploration of theoretical mechanisms and broader implications of the research findings would strengthen the proposal.

The proposal is generally well-written and organized, but some sections could benefit from improved clarity and conciseness. Major weaknesses: Occasional imprecise terminology and some repetitive elements detract from overall readability. Next band requirements: Improving clarity and precision in terminology and reducing redundancy would enhance the presentation quality.

evaluation.comments: Total score: 76.0/100. Academic level: Master-level. Major strengths: Clear identification of a relevant research problem.; Introduction of a hybrid MARL framework with potential for significant contributions. Major weaknesses: Insufficient operational definitions of key constructs.; Weak transitions and unsupported assumptions in logical coherence. Required improvements for true PhD-level quality: Enhance operational definitions and clarity of constructs.; Strengthen empirical justification for assumptions and connections between theory and methodology.; Provide a more critical synthesis of literature and articulate broader implications. Final verdict: The proposal demonstrates potential but lacks the depth and rigor expected at the PhD level, requiring significant improvements to achieve genuine research maturity.
